aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abiasaph.title: Abiasaph
abiasaph.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abiasaph.note: Youngest of Korah's three sons, and the head of one of the Korahite families. Chronicles spells him Ebiasaph. His descendants ended up as temple gatekeepers and singers, after Korah himself had led a rebellion against Moses and been destroyed for it.

abib.title: Abib
abib.note: It is the first month of the religious year, and it carries the exodus and Passover. After the exile people called it Nisan.

abihu.title: Abihu
abihu.about: Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abihu.note: Aaron's second son. He and his brother Nadab brought fire the Lord had not asked for and died on the spot, and Aaron was not allowed to mourn them in public.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

ahisamach.title: Ahisamach
ahisamach.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ahisamach.note: Father of Oholiab, the skilled craftsman from Dan who worked beside Bezalel on the tabernacle.

aholiab.title: Aholiab
aholiab.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aholiab.note: Oholiab of Dan, the skilled craftsman God appointed alongside Bezalel to make the tabernacle and its furnishings.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

amminadab.title: Amminadab
amminadab.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
amminadab.note: Two great lines run back to him. Aaron married his daughter Elisheba, and his son Nahshon stands in David's ancestry, so he sits in both the priestly and the royal genealogies.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

amram.title: Amram
amram.about: Moses' father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
amram.note: The father of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. He was a Levite and married his father's sister Jochebed, and beyond that little is recorded about him.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

assir-2.title: Assir
assir-2.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
assir-2.note: A descendant of Korah, in the Levite line at Exodus 6:24 and 1 Chronicles 6:22.

baal-zephon.title: Baal-zephon
baal-zephon.note: A landmark on the shore by the Israelites' last camp before they crossed the sea. Exodus names it in the crossing story and Numbers in the list of wilderness stops.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

bezaleel.title: Bezaleel
bezaleel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
bezaleel.note: God named him and filled him with his Spirit to design and build the tabernacle and everything in it, the ark of the covenant included. He is the first person in the Bible described as filled with the Spirit.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

canaanite-2.title: Canaanite
canaanite-2.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
canaanite-2.note: Exodus names him once, and he is a woman from the patriarchs.

carmi.title: Carmi
carmi.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
carmi.note: Reuben's son, whose family became one of the tribe's clans.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eleazar.title: Eleazar
eleazar.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eleazar.note: Aaron's third son. Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, and Eleazar became high priest after his father. He worked with Moses on the second census and with Joshua on dividing the land, and his line held the high priesthood for most of the history after.

eliezer.title: Eliezer
eliezer.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eliezer.note: Moses's second son. The name means my God is my help, and his descendants are counted among the Levites in Chronicles.

elim.title: Elim
elim.note: After the bitter water at Marah, Israel came to Elim, with twelve springs and seventy palm trees. It is commonly placed at Wadi Gharandal, an oasis on Sinai's western coast road that still grows palms.

elisheba.title: Elisheba
elisheba.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elisheba.note: Aaron's wife, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon. Her four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, were the first priestly line.

elizaphan.title: Elizaphan
elizaphan.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elizaphan.note: He led the Kohathite Levites in the wilderness. When Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, he was one of those who carried the bodies out.

elkanah-4.title: Elkanah
elkanah-4.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elkanah-4.note: Exodus and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.

etham.title: Etham
etham.note: Israel's third camp out of Egypt, on the edge of the wilderness. From there God turned Moses back toward Pi-hahiroth to draw Pharaoh after them. It was near the north end of the Gulf of Suez, but nobody knows exactly where.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gershom.title: Gershom
gershom.note: These verses are the census ones, Genesis 46:11, Exodus 6:16 and Numbers 3 and 4, where his family is counted and given its share of the tabernacle work. The note filed with them describes Moses's firstborn, born in Midian and named for a stranger there, who is a different man.

gershon.title: Gershon
gershon.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
gershon.note: Levi's eldest son. His descendants carried the tabernacle's coverings, curtains and hangings by cart through the wilderness. Exodus 2:22 and 18:3, filed under this name, belong to a different man.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

goshen.title: Goshen
goshen.note: Joseph settled Jacob and the family here, in the eastern Nile delta, and Israel lived and multiplied there until the exodus. Pithom and Rameses were inside it, and it is generally identified with the Wadi Tumilat.

hebron-2.title: Hebron
hebron-2.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hebron-2.note: Kohath's son, a Levite, and a clan of Levites came from him.

hezron-2.title: Hezron
hezron-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hezron-2.note: Reuben's son, listed with the family that went down to Egypt and again in Reuben's line in Exodus and Chronicles. He is a different man from Perez's son of the same name.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

horeb.title: Horeb
horeb.note: Another name for Sinai, where Moses met God at the burning bush and Israel received the law, and where Elijah later ran and heard God in a still, small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire.

hur.title: Hur
hur.about: Aaron's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hur.note: He helped Aaron hold up Moses's arms while Israel fought Amalek, since Israel won as long as those hands stayed up. When Moses went up Sinai for the law, Hur was left in charge with Aaron.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

ithamar.title: Ithamar
ithamar.about: Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ithamar.note: Aaron's youngest son. Two of his brothers died for offering unauthorized fire and Eleazar became high priest, and Ithamar was put over the Levites who carried and kept the tabernacle. Eli came from his line, which held the high priesthood for a while before it went back to Eleazar's line under Zadok.

izhar.title: Izhar
izhar.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
izhar.note: He was Kohath's son, and his own son Korah led the rebellion against Moses in the wilderness.

jachin.title: Jachin
jachin.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jachin.note: One of the men who went down to Egypt, and a clan is counted from him in the Numbers census. The same name, meaning "he shall establish", was given to one of the temple's two bronze pillars.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jah.title: Jah
jah.note: A short, poetic form of Yahweh, God's covenant name. It turns up mostly in the Psalms, and it is the end of Hallelujah, "praise Yah".

jamin.title: Jamin
jamin.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jamin.note: One of Simeon's sons, in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers and Chronicles. The name was common.

jehoshua.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua.about: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
jehoshua.note: Joshua, in the longer spelling. Moses's attendant and successor, and one of two from the generation out of Egypt who lived to enter the land. He took Israel over the Jordan, brought down Jericho and divided the land among the tribes. The name means Yahweh saves, the same name Greek renders Jesus.

jemuel.title: Jemuel
jemuel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jemuel.note: He was Simeon's eldest son and one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family, and the later census of Simeon's clans calls him Nemuel.

jether.title: Jether
jether.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
jether.note: An Ishmaelite, by the record's own label, carrying a name several men shared. Exodus 4:18 uses it for Jethro, Moses's father-in-law, and Gideon's eldest son had it too, the boy too frightened to kill the captured Midianite kings.

jochebed.title: Jochebed
jochebed.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jochebed.note: The mother of Miriam, Aaron and Moses, and Amram's wife. She hid Moses for three months, set him in a basket on the Nile, and was then paid to nurse her own son for Pharaoh's daughter.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kohath.title: Kohath
kohath.about: Levi's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kohath.note: Levi's second son. His descendants had the holiest work in the tabernacle, carrying the ark and the sacred furniture on poles, and even they would die if they touched those things.

korah.title: Korah
korah.about: Aaron's adversary living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
korah.note: A Levite who led a revolt against Moses and Aaron, with more than two hundred fifty leading Israelites behind him, all saying the whole community was holy and Moses had no special claim. The ground opened and took Korah and his family alive, and fire burned up the rest. Israel complained about it the very next day.

levi.title: Levi
levi.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levi.note: Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.

libni.title: Libni
libni.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
libni.note: Gershon's son, Levi's grandson, and the head of one of the Levitical clans.

mahli.title: Mahli
mahli.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
mahli.note: Merari's son and Levi's grandson. His family became one of the Levitical clans with work at the tabernacle.

marah.title: Marah
marah.note: Three days past the sea, the first water Israel found was too bitter to drink. Moses threw a piece of wood in at the Lord's word and it turned sweet, and God gave them a statute there and tested them. Many put it at Ain Hawarah in Sinai, a spring that is still brackish.

massah.title: Massah
massah.note: "Testing." Near Rephidim the Israelites ran out of water, quarrelled with Moses and demanded a drink, testing God even as he tested them. The place was also called Meribah, and what happened there became shorthand for a hard heart, used as a warning in Psalm 95 and again in Hebrews 3.

merari.title: Merari
merari.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
merari.note: Levi's third son. His descendants had the heavy parts of the tabernacle, the frames, bars, pillars and bases, which went by cart instead of being carried.

meribah-2.title: Meribah
meribah-2.note: The other Meribah, near Rephidim, from Israel's first complaint about water in Exodus 17. Moses' blessing in Deuteronomy and Psalm 95 both name it again.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

migdol.title: Migdol
migdol.note: "Tower," a fortified point on Egypt's northeastern border. One Migdol is on Israel's route to the crossing of the sea. Jeremiah names a Migdol where Jewish refugees settled in Egypt, and Ezekiel's "from Migdol to Syene" means the whole length of the country.

miriam.title: Miriam
miriam.about: Moses' sister living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
miriam.note: Moses and Aaron's older sister, and a prophetess. She watched over the baby Moses in the reeds of the Nile, and after the crossing of the sea she led Israel's women in song.

mishael-2.title: Mishael
mishael-2.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
mishael-2.note: Exodus and Leviticus name him twice, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

mushi.title: Mushi
mushi.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
mushi.note: Merari's son and Levi's grandson. His family became one of the Levitical clans serving at the tabernacle.

naashon.title: Naashon
naashon.note: Leader of Judah in the wilderness years, and Aaron's brother-in-law. David came from his line, and so does Jesus in Matthew's genealogy.

nadab.title: Nadab
nadab.about: Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
nadab.note: Aaron's eldest son. He and his brother Abihu offered unauthorised fire before the Lord and were struck dead.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nepheg-2.title: Nepheg
nepheg-2.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
nepheg-2.note: Exodus names him once, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.

non.title: Non
non.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
non.note: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim, more usually spelled Nun and hardly ever seen outside the phrase "Joshua son of Nun."

ohad.title: Ohad
ohad.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ohad.note: The third son of Simeon, one of Jacob's family who went down into Egypt. He is missing from the Simeonite clan lists in Numbers 26, so his line may have died out or been folded into another clan.

palestina.title: Palestina
palestina.note: The King James word for Philistia, the Philistines' strip of coast along the Mediterranean.

pallu.title: Pallu
pallu.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
pallu.note: Reuben's son. His descendants, the Palluites, were one of the clans counted in the wilderness.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

pharaoh-4.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-4.note: The Pharaoh who put Israel to forced labour on store cities. He then ordered the Hebrew baby boys thrown into the river. His own daughter pulled one of them out.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phinehas.title: Phinehas
phinehas.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phinehas.note: Aaron's grandson, Eleazar's son. When Israel was being struck by a plague for idolatry and sexual sin with Moabite women, Phinehas drove a spear through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, and the plague stopped.

pi-hahiroth.title: Pi-hahiroth
pi-hahiroth.note: Israel doubled back from Etham and camped here beside the sea, and Pharaoh's army came up behind them. It was here that Moses stretched out his hand over the water.

pithom.title: Pithom
pithom.note: The Israelites were forced to build it for Pharaoh as a store city before the exodus. The name comes from the Egyptian "Per-Atum." That means house of the sun-god Atum.

puah.title: Puah
puah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
puah.note: Pharaoh ordered her and Shiphrah, two Hebrew midwives, to kill the Israelite baby boys at birth. They feared God more than Pharaoh, let the boys live, and God rewarded them for it.

putiel.title: Putiel
putiel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
putiel.note: His daughter married Eleazar, Aaron's son, and their son was Phinehas. Putiel himself is a name and nothing more.

raamses.title: Raamses
raamses.note: The Israelites built Raamses, also spelled Rameses, as a store city for Pharaoh in the eastern Nile Delta, alongside Pithom. When they left Egypt, this is where they set out from.

raguel-2.title: Raguel
raguel-2.about: Midianite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
raguel-2.note: Exodus and Numbers name him twice, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

rephidim.title: Rephidim
rephidim.note: Israel camped here near Sinai and ran out of water. The people nearly stoned Moses, and he struck the rock at Horeb and water came out. Amalek attacked them at the same place.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

shaul-2.title: Shaul
shaul-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shaul-2.note: Genesis and 3 other books name him 4 times, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

shimeah-2.title: Shimeah
shimeah-2.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shimeah-2.note: Exodus and 2 other books name him 5 times, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.

shiphrah.title: Shiphrah
shiphrah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shiphrah.note: Pharaoh told the Hebrew midwives to kill the baby boys as they were born. Shiphrah and Puah would not do it, and God rewarded them.

shur.title: Shur
shur.note: The wilderness on Egypt's northeastern frontier, between Egypt and Philistia. The name probably comes from a wall the Egyptians built there against raiders. Hagar ran toward it when Sarah sent her away.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

sin.title: Sin
sin.note: Israel crossed the Wilderness of Sin after leaving Egypt, and when the people complained of hunger this is where the manna and the quail first came.

sinai.title: Sinai
sinai.note: Also called Horeb. Israel camped at the foot of the mountain for about a year after the exodus, and the law came down through Moses here.

succoth-2.title: Succoth
succoth-2.note: Israel's first campsite after leaving Egypt.

thummim.title: Thummim
thummim.note: Paired with the Urim in the high priest's breastpiece, and used the same way, to put a question to God.

uri.title: Uri
uri.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
uri.note: Bezalel's father. Bezalel was the craftsman God picked to build the tabernacle and its furnishings.

urim.title: Urim
urim.note: The Urim and Thummim sat in the high priest's breastpiece. They were used to put yes-or-no questions to God. How they actually worked, nobody knows.

uzziel.title: Uzziel
uzziel.about: Aaron's uncle living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
uzziel.note: Kohath's son, and Aaron's uncle. His descendants had their own duties at the tabernacle.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zerah.title: Zerah
zerah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zerah.note: Genesis and Exodus name him twice, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

zichri-10.title: Zichri
zichri-10.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zichri-10.note: A Levite of the wilderness generation, named once in the family list of Exodus 6.

zipporah.title: Zipporah
zipporah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zipporah.note: Moses's wife, Jethro's daughter. On the road back to Egypt the Lord sought to kill Moses, and Zipporah circumcised their son and touched Moses with the foreskin, and he lived. Scripture does not explain it.

zithri.title: Zithri
zithri.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
